bull_case: Continued repurchases at deep discounts can materially increase intrinsic value per share.
bear_case: If structural checkout erosion persists, even cheap buybacks may merely shrink a declining base.
thesis: Capital allocation is a major strength at current valuation. Repurchasing roughly $6B of stock over the trailing year near the current price is highly accretive if FCF is durable. The remaining question is whether management can also stabilize the underlying moat.

evidence.claim: No correction/restatement flag was reported in the FY2025 10-K.

counterevidence: Branded checkout competition remains intense and active-account growth is essentially flat, limiting evidence of a widening moat.
falsifiers: If transaction-margin dollars contract persistently, branded checkout resumes material share loss, or buybacks stop creating FCF/share growth, the thesis weakens.
